questions.question: Quantitative microscopy CANNOT quantify the following :
Interpretation of 3-D quantitative information from a 2-D structure or length or point analysis is called :
The difference between the light intensity of the specimen and its background is called :

Using a 40 × objective, 20 divisions on the eyepiece graticule correspond to 10 divisions on the stage micrometer. If one division of stage micrometer is 100 µm, what is the length of a single eyepiece graticule division at this magnification ?
What is the significance of using scale bar on a micrograph (in quantitative optical microscopy) ?

answers.a: It provides the total magnification used to capture the micrograph
answers.b: It is only required for electron microscopy images
answers.c: It shows the actual size of the objects and remains accurate even if the image is resized
answers.d: It indicates the refractive index of the medium surrounding the specimen
